As Indians, we are conditioned to chase after ‘the degree’. Many of us spend years taking and retaking entrance exams to get into our preferred colleges. Then, once we get there, we read countless textbooks and take countless assessments, so that years later, we can get a coveted degree that gives us the opportunity to join a company with a cushy job title and a high salary package.

Cybersecurity is a field that doesn’t operate by these rules. Sure, many professionals that work in this space have certifications, and the field itself, due to the mounting cybersecurity skills gap, has some of the highest salary packages seen across industries. Yet, when companies look to add to their internal cybersecurity teams, they are looking for lots of other tangibles and intangibles that go beyond the degree.

This is because cybersecurity is a fast-moving, combative industry. You face off perennially against cybercriminals, with each side continuously evolving by developing countermeasures for each other’s tactics. As a result, tactics that were relevant yesterday are often obsolete today. Moreover, in the current landscape, this is a field that is undergoing drastic shifts due to a phenomenon that is taking over almost every industry today.
The AI Conundrum In Cybersecurity Today

According to the CrowdStrike 2026 Global Threat Report, attacks from AI-enabled adversaries rose 89% year-on-year. Malicious AI has led to attacks increasing both in terms of volume and sophistication.
Defenders are increasingly incorporating AI into their strategies.

The Kiteworks State of AI Cybersecurity 2026 Report claims that 77% of organizations now use genAI or LLMs in their security stacks — often to handle alerts, noise and most other tasks that entry level professionals were hired to do.

Right at the outset, organizations are looking for high-judgment, high-character individuals that can work in sync with AI systems and stay composed in the face of increasingly complex attacks.

Unfortunately, many cybersecurity courses are still ill-suited to handle the nature of this evolving scenario. In fact, many of them continue to be purely theory-based, which is a fallacy in today’s world — by the time a cybersecurity curriculum is approved, printed and taught, parts of it are likely already obsolete due to the increasingly advanced tactics and countermeasures incorporated by cyberattackers today.

blogs.title: Securing Critical Infrastructure In An Era Of Expanded Attack Surfaces
blogs.excerpt: Critical infrastructure organizations face thousands of attacks every week. Drawing on CISA's 'Securing The Next 250' campaign, here are three tiers — mastering the basics, setting up safeguards and having a response plan — to secure them.
body: Securing Critical Infrastructure In An Era Of Expanded Attack Surfaces

Critical infrastructure organizations face thousands of attacks every week. Drawing on CISA's 'Securing The Next 250' campaign, here are three tiers — mastering the basics, setting up safeguards and having a response plan — to secure them.

As every organization gets populated with more users, more endpoints and more environments, it becomes harder and harder to maintain a holistic cybersecurity strategy. It becomes even harder when you are constantly bombarded by different types of cyberattacks — a scenario that gets more difficult if you decide to work for a critical infrastructure organization in the future. Take, for example, a recent report by Check Point that says organizations in India faced an average of 3,195 cyber incidents per week in 2025. When you narrow it down to critical infrastructure industries, in this case education, the figure balloons to 7,684 attacks per week.
The trend has continued in 2026, with several high-profile critical infrastructure entities being breached:
Bank of Baroda (July 2026) confirmed an account compromise, with certain data accessed and the scope still under review.
Tata Electronics (June 2026) confirmed a cybersecurity incident, saying its operations were unaffected.
A third-party contractor breach connected to the Kudankulam Nuclear Plant (July 2026) exposed sensitive project files.

Should you decide to work in the cybersecurity division of a critical infrastructure organization in the future, the implications are huge. For any normal organization, being struck by a successful cyberattack leads to financial and reputational damage. However, if a critical infrastructure organization gets hit, the livelihood of Indian citizens could be adversely affected. Lives could even be lost.

Seeing this heightened importance, CISA's campaign for Cybersecurity Awareness Month is 'Securing The Next 250' — taking America's 250th birthday as a basis for securing its critical infrastructure for the next 250 years. Many of the learnings from the campaign will hold you in good stead as you make your way into the world of cybersecurity.
As we see it, the campaign prescribes 3 tiers to truly securing a critical infrastructure organization.

Cybersecurity often involves advanced tactics & techniques to ward off attackers — yet sometimes, cyberattacks happen simply because we forget about the basics. Just incorporating these 4 essentials will help make your future organization a lot safer.
that can be managed with a password manager.
to secure all your accounts, preferably phishing-resistant modes of authentication like FIDO2 passkeys.
to keep constantly updating your business software.
Instead of ignoring phishing attempts, get all your enterprise stakeholders to
The National Cybersecurity Alliance's campaign for the month covers these points in greater detail — something we also cover in

Once these basics have been instilled, it's time to layer some safeguards on top of that to ensure that security is maintained while your stakeholders are going about doing their daily tasks. CISA's campaign prescribes three safeguards that can help you massively when it comes to maintaining a strong cybersecurity posture:

All the communications being conducted between all the stakeholders in your future organization — whether it's emails, chats or file sharing — must be encrypted to strengthen your defences against attacks.

Use mechanisms that enable you to continuously monitor all work activities taking place in your organization. Additionally, set up guardrails so that anomalies are immediately detected in the case of an impending cyberattack.

Should a cyberattack be successful, your operations can't stop — too much is at stake if you work for a critical infrastructure organization. When you backup critical information, recovery is faster & less stressful.

When you're getting attacked, every second counts for a critical infrastructure organization. Lives and livelihoods could be at risk, after all. Therefore, a watertight incident response plan is critical in helping you tackle all these threats in an efficient manner.
Here are all the stages to effectively responding & recovering from cyberthreats:

Most threats linger in systems for weeks or months before you realize they're there. The first thing to do is set up detection tools in conjunction with your continuous monitoring processes so that you can identify threats soon after they enter your systems.

Of course, a lot of the alerts that come into SOC dashboards end up being false positives, and dealing with that could waste a lot of your time. AI is helpful in filtering out the noise and delivering relevant alerts for you to act on.

Once you realize that a particular alert presents a clear danger, it is time to respond. Pre-determined response playbooks being carried out by AI systems could drastically cut the time it takes for you to isolate and respond to the threat at hand.

Finally, once the threat has been dealt with, it is important to learn from what has happened and ensure that it doesn't happen again in the future. Forensic investigations are critical to understanding these learnings and incorporating them to tackle future threats.

One thing to note — with the new DPDP requirements being set in place soon, you will have a 6-hour response window to inform the relevant authorities if a cyber incident has indeed taken place in your organization. Time is very much of the essence, after all.

blogs.title: Practical Ways Of Building A Strong Cybersecurity Culture In Your Future Organization
blogs.excerpt: During Cybersecurity Awareness Month, it's the simple habits that matter most. Here are four practical, India-focused behaviours — strong passwords, phishing-resistant MFA, reporting phishing, and patch management — to build a strong cybersecurity culture.
body: Practical Ways Of Building A Strong Cybersecurity Culture In Your Future Organization

During Cybersecurity Awareness Month, it's the simple habits that matter most. Here are four practical, India-focused behaviours — strong passwords, phishing-resistant MFA, reporting phishing, and patch management — to build a strong cybersecurity culture.
As you make your way into the world of cybersecurity, you will learn many advanced tactics & techniques to help you ward off cybercriminals. In fact, we teach many of them in all of
. But sometimes, in the fight against cybercrime, it's the simple things that count the most — the very same ones that we so often neglect.

This month, which happens to be Cybersecurity Awareness Month, the National Cybersecurity Alliance aims to course correct this through their 'Don't Make It Easy For Them' campaign. It emphasizes the fact that staying safe online isn't about making one perfect decision — it's about building habits and repeating them consistently. Just being aware and vigilant about these simple things will take you very far in your cybersecurity career.
The campaign promotes 4 major behaviours that we will take you through in this blog, with an India-centric outlook to each for your benefit:
Behaviour No. 1: Incorporate A Password Manager With Strong, Unique Passwords
India Context: 68% of Indian organisations cite credential theft as the leading way into cloud infrastructure.

Passwords are often a cyberattacker's preferred way of getting into enterprise systems, and frankly, many of us make it easy for them to do so. We often use simplistic passwords that are easy for hackers to obtain through either guesswork or brute force, then reuse it across multiple accounts. This is a situation ripe for credential theft, and NCA's campaign aims to correct these behaviours by prescribing the following tips:
Passwords should be at least 16 characters, a different one for every account.
Password managers should then be incorporated to make it easy for users logging into multiple accounts on a daily basis for their work.
Prioritize passwords for email accounts, as this is the recovery path for everything else.
Start moving away from passwords entirely, using passkeys and other forms of passwordless authentication.
India Context: 76.8% of Indian organisations suffered an identity-related breach in the past year.

Okta reports that Indian enterprises have a workforce MFA adoption of 89.4%, versus a 70% global average. Despite that, we're still getting breached. That in itself tells a story — adoption of MFA isn't a problem, quality is.

Continuing from all the themes mentioned in the first behaviour, the key to securing enterprises is to go passwordless and incorporate phishing-resistant methods of authentication that don't require much recall from users. Here is a scale of authentication factors in ascending order of phishing resistance:
Passkeys + Hardware Security Keys With FIDO2 Authentication
Behaviour 3: Don't Ignore Phishing — Recognize And Report It
India Context: 1 in 5 Indian families using UPI reported a fraud attempt, and 51% of victims didn't report it.
There are roughly 3.4 billion phishing attempts sent out every day worldwide. Some of them yield results, many of them fall between the cracks.
The key to building a solid cybersecurity culture in your future enterprise is to turn all your stakeholders
from your biggest vulnerability into your greatest asset

. To do that, you have to make them into active defenders — when they see a phishing attempt, they shouldn't ignore it. Instead, they should report it to you and other members of your team immediately.
When they ignore it, phishing attempts slip through the cracks. When they report it, your attempts become
that passes on to other enterprises — keeping both you and them secure in the process.
Behaviour 4: Use A Strong Patch Management Tool
India Context: Seqrite observed over 9.2 million network-based exploit scans and more than 8 million host-based exploit detections amongst Indian organisations between October 2024 to September 2025.

Your future enterprise will have dozens, if not hundreds, of work tools and software that require constant updates. The time between the update being available and you incorporating it is time that an attacker thrives on. Once a fix ships, attackers can study it, which is why unpatched systems are targeted so fast. A vendor survey recently revealed that about 81% of CIOs and CISOs delay patches to avoid interrupting business.
NCA has many tips on how to close this big gap:
Conduct automatic updates by default for phones, laptops, browsers and apps. Subsequently, do a monthly check for what auto-updates miss — components like routers, IoT devices and firmware.
Retire unsupported, end-of-life products that no longer receive fixes, because that makes them unsecure by default.
Incorporate a consolidated patch manager that helps you keep track of updates for all your workforce tools.

Why You Should Learn AI Skills

Across almost all industries, especially in the corporate space, knowledge of AI tools is becoming as standard as familiarity with Microsoft Word or Google Sheets. In fact, in the same India Skills Report, more than 90% of Indian professionals have already begun working with genAI tools.
There is a prevailing fear (and you may have it too) that AI will replace certain jobs. That statement is a fallacy — it won’t replace jobs but rather, tasks within jobs.

What that means is — AI may not replace your job, but someone with AI skills might. Therefore, if you’re looking to truly move forward in your career, learning AI skills becomes non-negotiable and, in turn, one of the best investments you can make right now.

The beauty of it is, learning AI doesn’t involve looking at lines and lines of cumbersome code. It just requires you to effectively talk to these machines, understand what they can do well (and what they can’t), and integrate them into your daily work. In fact, it’s already proven to have massive application in streamlining and simplifying core tasks in most industries:

Now, if you’re someone who’s looking to switch careers, you probably aren’t looking for one where you have to start from complete scratch — undertaking years of gaining long-term degrees and relevant work experience to start making your mark on the industry. You probably want a career that you can seamlessly transition to, with as little friction as possible.

Cybersecurity could be that career. In fact, so many pioneers currently working in the space end up transitioning from different careers, like you’re planning to. body: How To Know If Cybersecurity Is The Right Career For You
Last year, India faced over 265 million cyberattacks, with enterprises across the country having to deal with an average of 3,195 attacks per week. If any one of these attempts happened to find…

Last year, India faced over 265 million cyberattacks, with enterprises across the country having to deal with an average of 3,195 attacks per week. If any one of these attempts happened to find success, they had to shell out an average of ₹22 crore per data breach as part of the fallout.

There are a number of reasons why these adversaries are finding increasing success when it comes to infiltrating our enterprises: use of malicious AI, an explosion in different types of potentially vulnerable enterprise devices, but one of the main reasons is simply that there aren’t enough cyberdefenders to stop the cyberattackers. In fact, the field of Indian cybersecurity has one of the largest disparities, across industries, between demand and supply of talent.
The Ever-Widening Gap in Indian Cybersecurity
Currently available in India across enterprise defensive and offensive teams.
Estimated national demand across cloud security, SOC operations, and threat hunting.
Makes cybersecurity the single largest opportunity gap across all Indian STEM sectors.
This gap presents an incredible and unique opportunity for individuals like you to fill it.

, because the field of cybersecurity offers some of the highest salaries across job tiers, from starting level positions to higher level leadership roles. The massive financial and reputational damage that can result from a successful breach has led to Indian enterprises having higher budgets than ever for building their cybersecurity teams.

, because cybersecurity isn’t a traditional industry, and you don’t need 4-year degrees or a massive amount of work experience to make your way in and set yourself apart in this field. In fact, many of the best professionals in this space don’t study cybersecurity in college, and often come to this industry through different, diverse pathways.

It’s a perfect storm that you are primed to truly leverage. Yet, while we’ve hopefully answered the question of ‘is cybersecurity a good career?’, let’s now move up a level to ‘is cybersecurity a good career for you?’
The Hard & Soft Skills Required To Succeed In Cybersecurity

Cybersecurity doesn’t lend itself to traditional learning methods because it is a relatively new field that is constantly evolving. In fact, many of the tactics & techniques that were relevant a decade ago are obsolete today. Therefore, to truly succeed in this field, you need to possess an often rare mix of hard and soft skills.
Solid foundations in TCP/IP, DNS, firewalls, and basic Python/Bash scripting.
Global standards (NIST, ISO 27001) and local mandates (DPDP Rules, CERT-In guidelines).
Practical hands-on with SIEM platforms, IDS/IPS, and vulnerability scanners.
Mastering adversarial AI tools and automating defensive triage workflows.
Operating as an ethical custodian over highly sensitive corporate telemetry and intellectual property.
Translating deep technical vulnerability findings into clear business risk terms.
Proactively probing system edges and staying obsessed with emerging attacker TTPs.
Staying analytical and focused during active live breach containment incidents.
The Different Career Paths In Cybersecurity Today

While foundational skills serve as an entry point, cybersecurity is an increasingly sprawling industry. While executive roles like CISO exist at senior tiers, employers hiring entry and mid-tier talent want candidates who specialize in a defined domain.
Masterfully securing diverse digital infrastructure and modern enterprise cloud estates.
Embedding security into architectures from the ground up so resilience is built-in rather than bolted on.
Detecting, triaging, and neutralizing active adversary threats in real time before damage escalates.
Thinking like external adversaries to discover flaw surfaces before real cybercriminals exploit them.
How Do I Enter The Industry With The Highest Salary Possible?
Starting salaries in Indian cybersecurity typically range from ₹4–₹8 LPA annually, but four key accelerators consistently push candidates toward top pay bands:
Help you earn 15–25% higher compensation than uncertified applicants.
Proven ability to execute live labs and CTF exploits in risk-free environments.
DPDP compliance and CERT-In mandates have boosted GRC role demand by 40%.
Cloud security, active directory exploitation, and SOC telemetry specialists command significant market premiums.
